# Purpose

This notebook integrates the 2022 fiber, processing, and yarn measurements from the
same machine-harvested, microginned lint lots used for miniature spinning.

The analysis is designed to answer four questions:

1. Which initial fiber properties are associated with final yarn performance?
2. Are upper-tail fiber-length traits such as UHML, UQL(w), L5, and fibrogram
   upper-tail measures more informative than whole-distribution averages?
3. Do short-fiber content, fineness/maturity, card waste, or processing-stage
   changes help explain yarn outcomes?
4. Can the strong pair-specific yarn response observed for DP213 be linked to a
   distinctive fiber phenotype?

The formal inferential population is the 16 NIILs (64 field samples). Parents and
checks are retained only for descriptive correlations and figures.

Because only 64 formal NIIL observations are available, this notebook avoids large
"all predictors at once" models. Instead, it uses:

- prespecified fiber predictors;
- pairwise correlations;
- one-predictor-at-a-time design-adjusted models;
- a small number of biologically motivated multivariable models;
- exploratory pair-level QTL-difference analyses.

The 2022 audit identifies the microgin HVI, microgin AFIS, microgin fibrogram,
classing-office HVI, MiniSpin AFIS, and yarn measurements as matched observations
from the 92-sample experiment. The raw workbook is therefore read by verified
column position to avoid duplicate variable-name collisions.

```{r required-packages}
  !vapply(
```

# 3. Locate input files

The cleaned yarn table is required.

The original 2022 MiniSpin analysis workbook is used only for the fiber blocks.
The script automatically checks all sheets and identifies the one containing
approximately 92 rows and at least 114 columns.

```{r locate-input-files}
yarn_file <- file.path(
  paths$data_processed,
  "yarn_2022_sample_level_clean.csv"
)

raw_matches <- list.files(
  paths$data_raw,
  pattern = "^2022 UGA Mini-Spin Raw Data.*\\.xlsx$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE
)

if (!file.exists(yarn_file)) {
  stop(
    "Missing cleaned yarn file:\n",
    yarn_file
  )
}

if (length(raw_matches) == 0) {
  stop(
    "Could not find the 2022 raw MiniSpin workbook in 02_data_raw.\n",
    "Expected a filename beginning with '2022 UGA Mini-Spin Raw Data'."
  )
}

if (length(raw_matches) > 1) {
  stop(
    "More than one 2022 raw MiniSpin workbook was found:\n",
    paste(
      basename(raw_matches),
      collapse = "\n"
    )
  )
}

raw_file <- raw_matches[[1]]

input_file_audit <- tibble::tibble(
  source = c(
    "Cleaned yarn",
    "2022 raw fiber/yarn workbook"
  ),
  file = c(
    basename(yarn_file),
    basename(raw_file)
  ),
  exists = c(
    file.exists(yarn_file),
    file.exists(raw_file)
  )
)

input_file_audit
```

# 4. Identify the 92 × 114 analysis sheet

```{r identify-analysis-sheet}
raw_sheets <- readxl::excel_sheets(
  raw_file
)

sheet_dimensions <- purrr::map_dfr(
  raw_sheets,
  function(sheet_name) {

    test_data <- tryCatch(
      readxl::read_excel(
        raw_file,
        sheet = sheet_name,
        n_max = 100,
        .name_repair = "unique_quiet"
      ),
      error = function(e) {
        NULL
      }
    )

    if (is.null(test_data)) {
      return(
        tibble::tibble(
          sheet = sheet_name,
          rows_read = NA_integer_,
          columns = NA_integer_
        )
      )
    }

    tibble::tibble(
      sheet = sheet_name,
      rows_read = nrow(test_data),
      columns = ncol(test_data)
    )
  }
)

sheet_dimensions

candidate_sheets <- sheet_dimensions |>
  dplyr::filter(
    rows_read >= 90,
    columns >= 114
  )

if (nrow(candidate_sheets) != 1) {
  stop(
    "The script could not uniquely identify the 92-sample, 114-column analysis sheet.\n",
    "Review 'sheet_dimensions' above."
  )
}

analysis_sheet <- candidate_sheets$sheet[[1]]

message(
  "Using raw analysis sheet: ",
  analysis_sheet
)
```

# 5. Import raw 2022 analysis table by column position

The original audit documented 114 columns:

- 1–2: genotype and replication;
- 3–36: boll-sample fiber blocks;
- 37–42: Cotton Incorporated HVI on microgin samples;
- 43–63: Cotton Incorporated AFIS on microgin samples;
- 64–70: Texas Tech fibrogram on microgin samples;
- 71–74: classing-office HVI;
- 75–95: MiniSpin AFIS;
- 96–114: yarn traits.

Only the matched microgin/fibrogram/classing/MiniSpin fiber blocks are carried
forward here.

```{r import-raw-data}
raw_2022_unfiltered <- readxl::read_excel(
  raw_file,
  sheet = analysis_sheet,
  .name_repair = "unique_quiet"
)

if (ncol(raw_2022_unfiltered) < 114) {
  stop(
    "Expected at least 114 columns in the raw analysis table; found ",
    ncol(raw_2022_unfiltered),
    "."
  )
}

# The workbook may contain one extra title/header/spacer row in addition to the
# 92 biological observations. Evaluate columns 1 and 2 outside dplyr so numeric
# column positions can be used safely.
.raw_genotype_check <- stringr::str_trim(
  as.character(
    raw_2022_unfiltered[[1]]
  )
)

.raw_rep_check <- suppressWarnings(
  as.integer(
    raw_2022_unfiltered[[2]]
  )
)

.keep_raw_row <- (
  !is.na(.raw_genotype_check) &
  .raw_genotype_check != "" &
  !is.na(.raw_rep_check)
)

raw_2022 <- raw_2022_unfiltered[
  .keep_raw_row,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

raw_row_audit <- tibble::tibble(
  rows_read_from_sheet =
    nrow(raw_2022_unfiltered),
  rows_retained_as_observations =
    nrow(raw_2022),
  rows_removed_as_nondata =
    nrow(raw_2022_unfiltered) -
    nrow(raw_2022)
)

raw_row_audit

if (nrow(raw_2022) != 92) {
  stop(
    "After removing non-data rows, expected 92 biological observations; found ",
    nrow(raw_2022),
    ". Review 'raw_2022_unfiltered' and 'raw_row_audit'."
  )
}
```

# 7. Standardize genotype labels for joining

```{r standardize-genotype}
standardize_raw_genotype <- function(x) {

  x <- as.character(x)
  x <- stringr::str_replace(x, "_01$", "")
  x <- stringr::str_replace_all(x, "[^A-Za-z0-9]", "")

  dplyr::case_when(
    x == "GA2018001" ~ "GA201800",
    x == "GA2018081" ~ "GA201808",
    TRUE ~ x
  )
}

fiber_2022 <- fiber_2022 |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    genotype = standardize_raw_genotype(genotype_raw)
  )
```

# 8. Import cleaned yarn and join by genotype × field replication

```{r join-fiber-yarn}
yarn_2022 <- readr::read_csv(
  yarn_file,
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    genotype = as.character(genotype),
    rep_raw = suppressWarnings(as.integer(field_rep_inferred))
  )

fiber_key_audit <- fiber_2022 |>
  dplyr::count(
    genotype,
    rep_raw
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    n != 1
  )

if (nrow(fiber_key_audit) > 0) {
  stop(
    "The raw fiber table is not unique by genotype × replication."
  )
}

yarn_key_audit <- yarn_2022 |>
  dplyr::count(
    genotype,
    rep_raw
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    n != 1
  )

if (nrow(yarn_key_audit) > 0) {
  stop(
    "The cleaned yarn table is not unique by genotype × replication."
  )
}

fiber_yarn <- yarn_2022 |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    fiber_2022,
    by = c(
      "genotype",
      "rep_raw"
    )
  )

join_audit <- fiber_yarn |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    rows = dplyr::n(),
    matched_fiber_rows = sum(!is.na(hvi_microgin_UHML)),
    unmatched_fiber_rows = sum(is.na(hvi_microgin_UHML))
  )

join_audit

readr::write_csv(
  join_audit,
  file.path(integration_table_dir, "fiber_yarn_join_audit.csv"),
  na = ""
)

if (
  nrow(fiber_yarn) != 92 ||
  any(is.na(fiber_yarn$hvi_microgin_UHML))
) {
  stop(
    "The fiber-to-yarn join was not complete. Review genotype standardization and replication."
  )
}
```

# 9. Optionally integrate cleaned AFIS processing-stage data

If `afis_2022_clean_wide.csv` is available, processing-stage changes are added.
The notebook does not fail if this file is absent; the initial-fiber/yarn analysis
still runs.

```{r optional-afis-stage-data}
afis_stage_file <- file.path(
  paths$data_processed,
  "afis_2022_clean_wide.csv"
)

afis_stage_available <- file.exists(
  afis_stage_file
)

afis_stage_available

if (afis_stage_available) {

  afis_stage <- readr::read_csv(
    afis_stage_file,
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

  required_stage_columns <- c(
    "field_sample_id",
    "Bale_UQL_w",
    "Sliver_UQL_w",
    "Bale_L5_n",
    "Sliver_L5_n",
    "Bale_SFC_n",
    "Sliver_SFC_n",
    "Bale_Nep_count",
    "Sliver_Nep_count"
  )

  missing_stage_columns <- setdiff(
    required_stage_columns,
    names(afis_stage)
  )

  if (length(missing_stage_columns) > 0) {

    warning(
      "AFIS stage file exists but does not contain all expected clean columns. ",
      "Stage-change predictors will be skipped.\nMissing: ",
      paste(
        missing_stage_columns,
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )

    afis_stage_available <- FALSE

  } else {

    afis_stage_small <- afis_stage |>
      dplyr::transmute(
        field_sample_id = as.character(field_sample_id),

        bale_UQLw = Bale_UQL_w,
        sliver_UQLw = Sliver_UQL_w,
        delta_UQLw = Sliver_UQL_w - Bale_UQL_w,

        bale_L5 = Bale_L5_n,
        sliver_L5 = Sliver_L5_n,
        delta_L5 = Sliver_L5_n - Bale_L5_n,

        bale_SFCn = Bale_SFC_n,
        sliver_SFCn = Sliver_SFC_n,
        delta_SFCn = Sliver_SFC_n - Bale_SFC_n,

        bale_Neps = Bale_Nep_count,
        sliver_Neps = Sliver_Nep_count,
        delta_Neps = Sliver_Nep_count - Bale_Nep_count
      )

    fiber_yarn <- fiber_yarn |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        field_sample_id = as.character(field_sample_id)
      ) |>
      dplyr::left_join(
        afis_stage_small,
        by = "field_sample_id"
      )
  }
}
```

# 10. Create formal NIIL integration population

```{r formal-population}
fiber_yarn <- fiber_yarn |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    background = factor(
      background,
      levels = c(
        "Acala",
        "Deltapine",
        "Georgia",
        "Paymaster"
      )
    ),
    qtl_status = factor(
      qtl_status,
      levels = c(
        "Negative",
        "Positive",
        "Parent_Check"
      )
    ),
    field_rep = factor(field_rep_inferred),
    pair_id = interaction(
      background,
      nil_set,
      drop = TRUE
    )
  )

integration_formal <- fiber_yarn |>
  dplyr::filter(
    material_type == "NIIL",
    qtl_status %in% c(
      "Negative",
      "Positive"
    )
  ) |>
  droplevels()

formal_audit <- tibble::tibble(
  check = c(
    "Matched 2022 samples",
    "Formal NIIL samples",
    "NIIL genotypes",
    "NIL pairs"
  ),
  result = c(
    nrow(fiber_yarn),
    nrow(integration_formal),
    dplyr::n_distinct(integration_formal$genotype),
    dplyr::n_distinct(integration_formal$pair_id)
  )
)

formal_audit

readr::write_csv(
  formal_audit,
  file.path(integration_table_dir, "fiber_yarn_formal_population_audit.csv"),
  na = ""
)
```

# 11. Prespecify fiber predictors

This list deliberately prioritizes biologically interpretable, nonredundant
measurements.

```{r predictor-list}
initial_fiber_predictors <- c(
  "hvi_microgin_UHML",
  "hvi_microgin_STR",
  "hvi_microgin_MIC",
  "afis_microgin_UQLw",
  "afis_microgin_L5",
  "afis_microgin_SFCn",
  "afis_microgin_Fine",
  "afis_microgin_MatRatio",
  "fibrogram_microgin_UQLf",
  "fibrogram_microgin_SFCf"
)

supporting_fiber_predictors <- c(
  "hvi_microgin_UI",
  "hvi_microgin_SFI",
  "afis_microgin_Lw",
  "afis_microgin_Ln",
  "afis_microgin_LwCV",
  "afis_microgin_LnCV",
  "afis_microgin_Neps",
  "hvi_classing_UHML",
  "hvi_classing_STR",
  "minispin_afis_UQLw",
  "minispin_afis_L5",
  "minispin_afis_SFCn",
  "minispin_afis_Fine",
  "minispin_afis_MatRatio"
)

processing_predictors <- c(
  "card_waste_pct",
  "actual_yarn_count_ne"
)

if (afis_stage_available) {
  processing_predictors <- c(
    processing_predictors,
    "delta_UQLw",
    "delta_L5",
    "delta_SFCn",
    "delta_Neps",
    "sliver_UQLw",
    "sliver_SFCn"
  )
}

all_fiber_predictors <- unique(
  c(
    initial_fiber_predictors,
    supporting_fiber_predictors,
    processing_predictors
  )
)
```

# 14. Pearson correlations: all 92 samples

These correlations are descriptive because parents/checks are included.

```{r correlations-all92}
make_correlation_table <- function(
  data,
  predictors,
  outcomes,
  analysis_label
) {

  purrr::map_dfr(
    outcomes,
    function(outcome) {

      purrr::map_dfr(
        predictors,
        function(predictor) {

          x <- data[[predictor]]
          y <- data[[outcome]]

          complete <- stats::complete.cases(
            x,
            y
          )

          if (sum(complete) < 4) {
            return(
              tibble::tibble()
            )
          }

          test <- stats::cor.test(
            x[complete],
            y[complete],
            method = "pearson"
          )

          tibble::tibble(
            analysis = analysis_label,
            yarn_trait = outcome,
            fiber_predictor = predictor,
            n = sum(complete),
            r = unname(test$estimate),
            p_value = test$p.value
          )
        }
      )
    }
  )
}

correlations_all92 <- make_correlation_table(
  data = fiber_yarn,
  predictors = all_fiber_predictors,

  analysis_label = "All 92 samples"

  dplyr::group_by(
```

# 17. Design-adjusted one-predictor mixed models

For each fiber predictor and yarn outcome:

`Yarn = Background + QTL + FieldRep + standardized fiber predictor + (1 | pair_id)`

The fiber coefficient asks whether a fiber measurement predicts yarn performance
after accounting for the basic NIIL design.

These models are preferable to interpreting raw correlations alone.

```{r adjusted-model-function}
fit_adjusted_fiber_model <- function(
  outcome,
  predictor
) {

  model_data <- integration_formal |>
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(.data[[outcome]]),
      !is.na(.data[[predictor]])
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      predictor_z = as.numeric(
        scale(.data[[predictor]])
      )
    ) |>
    droplevels()

  formula_object <- stats::as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ background + qtl_status + field_rep + ",
      "predictor_z + (1 | pair_id)"
    )
  )

  fit <- tryCatch(
    lmerTest::lmer(
      formula_object,
      data = model_data,
      REML = TRUE,
      control = lme4::lmerControl(
        optimizer = "bobyqa",
        optCtrl = list(
          maxfun = 100000
        )
      )
    ),
    error = function(e) {
      e
    }
  )

  list(
    outcome = outcome,
    predictor = predictor,
    n = nrow(model_data),
    model = fit
  )
}
```

# 19. Extract standardized predictor effects

```{r extract-adjusted-effects}
extract_predictor_effect <- function(result) {

  if (inherits(result$model, "error")) {
    return(
      tibble::tibble(
        yarn_trait = result$outcome,
        fiber_predictor = result$predictor,
        n = result$n,
        estimate_per_sd = NA_real_,
        se = NA_real_,
        df = NA_real_,
        t_value = NA_real_,
        p_value = NA_real_,
        singular = NA,
        model_error = conditionMessage(result$model)
      )
    )
  }

  coef_table <- as.data.frame(
    summary(result$model)$coefficients
  )

  if (!"predictor_z" %in% rownames(coef_table)) {
    return(
      tibble::tibble(
        yarn_trait = result$outcome,
        fiber_predictor = result$predictor,
        n = result$n,
        estimate_per_sd = NA_real_,
        se = NA_real_,
        df = NA_real_,
        t_value = NA_real_,
        p_value = NA_real_,
        singular = lme4::isSingular(
          result$model,
          tol = 1e-4
        ),
        model_error = "predictor_z coefficient not found"
      )
    )
  }

  row <- coef_table["predictor_z", , drop = FALSE]

  tibble::tibble(
    yarn_trait = result$outcome,
    fiber_predictor = result$predictor,
    n = result$n,
    estimate_per_sd = row[["Estimate"]],
    se = row[["Std. Error"]],
    df = row[["df"]],
    t_value = row[["t value"]],
    p_value = row[["Pr(>|t|)"]],
    singular = lme4::isSingular(
      result$model,
      tol = 1e-4
    ),
    model_error = NA_character_
  )
}

    )
  ) |>

adjusted_fiber_effects |>

  )
```

# 21. Small biologically motivated tenacity models

Three compact models are compared:

1. HVI model: UHML + bundle strength + MIC;
2. AFIS model: UQL(w) + SFC(n) + fineness + maturity ratio;
3. fibrogram model: UQLf + SFCf.

All predictors are standardized so coefficients are directly comparable.

```{r multivariable-helper}
fit_small_tenacity_model <- function(
  predictor_names,
  model_name
) {

  model_data <- integration_formal |>
    dplyr::select(
      yarn_tenacity_cn_tex,
      background,
      qtl_status,
      field_rep,
      pair_id,
      dplyr::all_of(
        predictor_names
      )
    ) |>
    tidyr::drop_na() |>
    droplevels()

  for (predictor in predictor_names) {
    model_data[[paste0(predictor, "_z")]] <-
      as.numeric(
        scale(
          model_data[[predictor]]
        )
      )
  }

  standardized_predictors <- paste0(
    predictor_names,
    "_z"
  )

  formula_object <- stats::as.formula(
    paste(
      "yarn_tenacity_cn_tex ~ background + qtl_status + field_rep +",
      paste(
        standardized_predictors,
        collapse = " + "
      ),
      "+ (1 | pair_id)"
    )
  )

  fit <- lmerTest::lmer(
    formula_object,
    data = model_data,
    REML = FALSE,
    control = lme4::lmerControl(
      optimizer = "bobyqa",
      optCtrl = list(
        maxfun = 100000
      )
    )
  )

  list(
    name = model_name,
    predictors = predictor_names,
    n = nrow(model_data),
    model = fit
  )
}
```

```{r fit-small-tenacity-models}
tenacity_hvi_model <- fit_small_tenacity_model(
  predictor_names = c(
    "hvi_microgin_UHML",
    "hvi_microgin_STR",
    "hvi_microgin_MIC"
  ),
  model_name = "HVI"
)

tenacity_afis_model <- fit_small_tenacity_model(
  predictor_names = c(
    "afis_microgin_UQLw",
    "afis_microgin_SFCn",
    "afis_microgin_Fine",
    "afis_microgin_MatRatio"
  ),
  model_name = "AFIS"
)

tenacity_fibrogram_model <- fit_small_tenacity_model(
  predictor_names = c(
    "fibrogram_microgin_UQLf",
    "fibrogram_microgin_SFCf"
  ),
  model_name = "Fibrogram"
)

tenacity_small_models <- list(
  HVI = tenacity_hvi_model,
  AFIS = tenacity_afis_model,
  Fibrogram = tenacity_fibrogram_model
)
```

# 24. Processing-enhanced tenacity model

This model asks whether actual yarn count and card waste add information beyond
initial upper-tail fiber length.

Actual yarn count is interpreted cautiously because it is itself a downstream
processing outcome associated with qFL-Chr.25.

```{r processing-tenacity-model}
processing_model_data <- integration_formal |>
  dplyr::select(
    yarn_tenacity_cn_tex,
    background,
    qtl_status,
    field_rep,
    pair_id,
    hvi_microgin_UHML,
    afis_microgin_UQLw,
    afis_microgin_SFCn,
    card_waste_pct,
    actual_yarn_count_ne
  ) |>
  tidyr::drop_na() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    hvi_UHML_z = as.numeric(
      scale(hvi_microgin_UHML)
    ),
    afis_UQLw_z = as.numeric(
      scale(afis_microgin_UQLw)
    ),
    afis_SFCn_z = as.numeric(
      scale(afis_microgin_SFCn)
    ),
    card_waste_z = as.numeric(
      scale(card_waste_pct)
    ),
    actual_count_z = as.numeric(
      scale(actual_yarn_count_ne)
    )
  ) |>
  droplevels()

tenacity_processing_model <- lmerTest::lmer(
  yarn_tenacity_cn_tex ~
    background +
    qtl_status +
    field_rep +
    hvi_UHML_z +
    afis_UQLw_z +
    afis_SFCn_z +
    card_waste_z +
    actual_count_z +
    (1 | pair_id),
  data = processing_model_data,
  REML = FALSE,
  control = lme4::lmerControl(
    optimizer = "bobyqa",
    optCtrl = list(
      maxfun = 100000
    )
  )
)

tenacity_processing_coefficients <- broom.mixed::tidy(
  tenacity_processing_model,
  effects = "fixed"
)

tenacity_processing_coefficients
```

# 26. Pair-level QTL differences

For each of the eight NIIL pairs, QTL-positive minus QTL-negative differences are
calculated for fiber predictors and yarn outcomes.

This exploratory analysis asks whether NIIL pairs showing a larger fiber response
also show a larger yarn response.

With only eight pairs, these results should be interpreted descriptively.

```{r pair-level-differences}
pair_variables <- unique(
  c(
    initial_fiber_predictors,
    processing_predictors,
    primary_yarn_outcomes
  )
)

pair_qtl_means <- integration_formal |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    background,
    nil_set,
    qtl_status
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::all_of(
        pair_variables
      ),
      ~ mean(
        .x,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = qtl_status,
    values_from = dplyr::all_of(
      pair_variables
    ),
    names_glue = "{.value}_{qtl_status}"
  )

pair_qtl_differences <- pair_qtl_means

for (v in pair_variables) {
  pair_qtl_differences[[paste0("delta_", v)]] <-
    pair_qtl_differences[[paste0(v, "_Positive")]] -
    pair_qtl_differences[[paste0(v, "_Negative")]]
}

pair_qtl_differences
```

# 27. Pair-level fiber-change versus tenacity-change correlations

Spearman correlations are used because there are only eight NIL pairs.

```{r pair-level-tenacity-correlations}
pair_tenacity_correlations <- purrr::map_dfr(
  initial_fiber_predictors,
  function(predictor) {

    x_name <- paste0(
      "delta_",
      predictor
    )

    y_name <- "delta_yarn_tenacity_cn_tex"

    x <- pair_qtl_differences[[x_name]]
    y <- pair_qtl_differences[[y_name]]

    complete <- stats::complete.cases(
      x,
      y
    )

    if (sum(complete) < 5) {
      return(
        tibble::tibble()
      )
    }

    test <- suppressWarnings(
      stats::cor.test(
        x[complete],
        y[complete],
        method = "spearman",
        exact = FALSE
      )
    )

    tibble::tibble(
      fiber_predictor = predictor,
      n_pairs = sum(complete),
      spearman_rho = unname(test$estimate),
      p_value = test$p.value
    )
  }
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    fdr_p = stats::p.adjust(
      p_value,
      method = "BH"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    fdr_p,
    p_value
  )

pair_tenacity_correlations

readr::write_csv(
  pair_tenacity_correlations,
  file.path(integration_table_dir, "fiber_yarn_pair_tenacity_correlations.csv"),
  na = ""
)
```

```{r save-tables}
  "fiber_yarn_pair_qtl_differences.csv" =
    pair_qtl_differences,

  "fiber_yarn_pair_tenacity_correlations.csv" =
    pair_tenacity_correlations,

  "fiber_yarn_DP213_difference_summary.csv" =
    dp213_difference_summary
)

purrr::iwalk(
  output_tables,
  function(data, file_name) {

    readr::write_csv(
      data,
      file.path(
        integration_table_dir,
        file_name
      ),
      na = ""
    )
  }
)
```

# 34. Final analysis audit

```{r final-audit}
final_integration_audit <- tibble::tibble(
  check = c(
    "Matched samples",
    "Formal NIIL samples",
    "Initial fiber predictors",
    "All fiber/processing predictors",
    "Primary yarn outcomes",
    "Raw correlation tests, formal NIILs",
    "Adjusted fiber-yarn models attempted",
    "Adjusted models with numeric predictor p-value",
    "Adjusted models singular",
    "AFIS processing-stage data included",
    "NIL pairs in pair-difference analysis"
  ),
  result = c(
    nrow(fiber_yarn),
    nrow(integration_formal),
    length(initial_fiber_predictors),
    length(all_fiber_predictors),
    length(primary_yarn_outcomes),
    nrow(correlations_formal64),
    nrow(adjusted_model_grid),
    sum(!is.na(adjusted_fiber_effects$p_value)),
    sum(
      adjusted_fiber_effects$singular,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    as.integer(afis_stage_available),
    nrow(pair_qtl_differences)
  )
)

final_integration_audit

readr::write_csv(
  final_integration_audit,
  file.path(
    integration_table_dir,
    "fiber_yarn_final_integration_audit.csv"
  ),
  na = ""
)
```
